original_test_intent: Prove that the approved platform, hypervisor and guest stack can enable and disable SR-IOV, create the intended virtual functions and expose usable VF devices to the correct guest without resource, isolation or recovery errors.
original_method: Preserve the BIOS/host/hypervisor/guest baseline, apply the approved BIOS SR-IOV/IOMMU and VF configuration, reboot as required, correlate PF/VF identities from host through assignment to the guest, exercise the project-required guest use case, then restore the approved enable/disable final state.
manual_activity: The platform and virtualization owners define the PF/VF and guest matrix, approve BIOS/hypervisor changes and supervise reboots, assignment, guest installation/networking and rollback; automation collects and correlates evidence.
required_inputs: SUT/BIOS/CPU/chipset, PF PCI identity and SR-IOV capability
Exact BIOS SR-IOV and IOMMU settings plus expected enable/disable states
Supported host kernel, IOMMU groups, driver and hypervisor version/configuration
Approved VF count, resource budget, PF-to-VF-to-guest mapping and network/isolation policy
Guest image, installation state, driver and functional VF acceptance workload
Maintenance window, baseline, final state, OOB console and rollback/recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Preserve complete BIOS, PF/VF, IOMMU, hypervisor, guest and network baseline before changes
Require approval before BIOS, VF-count, assignment, guest or network changes and reboots
Do not expose credentials through sshpass or disable host identity verification
Never infer a safe VF count from `sriov_totalvfs`; enforce the approved resource budget
Stop on IOMMU faults, PF/VF identity mismatch, resource exhaustion, isolation loss or boot/network impact
Do not automatically retry assignment or add VFs after failure
Restore the approved BIOS/VF/guest/network final state through the validated rollback path
agent_execution_scope: Validate the platform matrix, PF identity, capability, resource and approval inputs
Collect complete host capability, IOMMU and current PF/VF baseline through protected access
Assist with the approved configuration sequence but not authorize BIOS or production assignment changes
Correlate VF PCI identity, driver and IOMMU group from host/hypervisor to the intended guest
Collect guest inventory plus project-approved VF functional/network evidence
Compare enable, disable and restored states without issuing the verdict
engineer_actions: Approve BIOS/IOMMU, VF count, assignment, guest and network/isolation design
Supervise state changes, reboots and guest installation/configuration
Resolve resource, driver, isolation or recovery failures before further mutation
Review end-to-end VF evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lspci`, IOMMU logs and sriov_totalvfs are useful host observations, but the grep-only unsafe SSH command cannot prove configured sriov_numvfs, hypervisor assignment, correct guest identity, driver binding or functional isolation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through protected access, collect complete PF/VF PCI capability, `sriov_totalvfs` and `sriov_numvfs`, IOMMU groups/logs, hypervisor assignment and matching guest inventory/status; perform writes only in the owner-approved sequence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Enable/disable scope, guest-install and guest-VF Criteria, no-script status and 60/420-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: PROJECT SR-IOV TOPOLOGY AND CONTROLLED CONFIGURATION REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat PF capability, VF instantiation, hypervisor assignment and guest usability as four separately evidenced stages tied by immutable PCI identities and the approved matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds resource/isolation constraints, identity correlation, complete enable/disable state transitions and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A `Virtual Function` string on the host can exist even when no VF is assigned to the intended guest or when its driver/network path is unusable.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: VF creation and pass-through can alter PF capacity, IOMMU isolation and multiple guests' networking; the blast radius is broader than the selected VM.

project_override_considerations: If guest OS installation is pre-provisioned rather than performed in this run, the Project must provide immutable image/driver provenance and explicitly approve that substitution while preserving the guest-boot and VF-usability Criteria.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/host/hypervisor/guest/PF identity, project VF matrix, approvals and pre-change baseline
Exact BIOS SR-IOV/IOMMU settings and controlled reboot/activation record
Complete PF capability, totalvfs/numvfs, VF PCI/IOMMU/driver and resource evidence
Hypervisor assignment mapping and matching guest device/driver inventory
Guest installation/provenance and project-approved VF usability/network/isolation results
Disable/rollback/final-state audit, relevant errors and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require SR-IOV enable/disable plus guest VF presence. Device, count, hypervisor and guest details are missing project inputs rather than conflicting source intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The required platform, hypervisor, guest, VF and recovery matrix is finite and can be supplied. Execution remains gated until it is approved.

review_improvement: Extends DeepSeek's host-only capability check into a controlled BIOS-to-guest SR-IOV lifecycle with identity, resource, isolation and rollback evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: SR-IOV success has distinct layers: hardware advertises capacity, the host instantiates VFs, the hypervisor assigns one, and the guest binds and uses it. Evidence from one layer cannot prove the next because a VF may exist yet remain unassigned, driverless or outside the intended isolation domain.
